title: The bus burns in Portsmouth, Ohio
summary: In April 1934 the band bus burned while they ate; the bass and drums were lost but the music and clothes were saved by the driver.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Tell us about that bus fire. Where was that and when was that, and exactly what happened?
Oh, that happened in Portsmouth, Ohio. I told you this, I think, once before...
We didn't have it on tape, though.
We came in there to play a dance, and we parked our bus in the back of a restaurant, so we get our rooms. We were getting rooms. So while we was there eating...

He was gone, yeah. This was '34. So somebody came running in the place where he was in, and said, "Man, you'all's bus is on fire." We went out there, and man, the bus was about half burned up. Burned up Dan's bass, Debo's drums. Only thing it didn't burn up was the music. It saved that. And it didn't burn up... We had a big rack on the top of the bus where everybody had their handbags and their clothes and things like that. Some of them had taken them down. Didn't nobody's clothes get burned. While it was burning... We had a white fellow who was driving the bus, and he ran up there on the top, and threw everybody's bags off. So the clothes wasn't burned, but the bus got burned.
